samples.summary: `master.placeholderStyles.{fontSize,lineHeight}` is a peer-writable numeric that reaches the exact sink the new bands guard, and it is read unbanded — the change bands slides/elements/notes/layouts but skips `masters`.
samples.evidence: `read()` does `const masters = yorkieToPlain<Master[]>(rootAny.masters);` (packages/frontend/src/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.ts:465) with no band, while the two lines above it deliberately band `layouts` via `bandLayoutNumerics` and the slide walk bands every element. `Master.placeholderStyles` carries `fontSize` and `lineHeight` (packages/slides/src/model/master.ts:4-34), and those values are copied *verbatim into a docs `Block`* by `seedPlaceholderBlocks` — `inlines[0].style.fontSize = style.fontSize` and `style.lineHeight = style.lineHeight` (packages/slides/src/model/placeholder-blocks.ts:30,38) — which is precisely the `fontSize`/`lineHeight` pair `bandBlockNumerics`/`normalizeFontSize`/`normalizeLineHeight` were added to bound. The same value is also multiplied straight into a canvas font at packages/slides/src/view/canvas/text-renderer.ts:362 (`ctx.font = `${style.fontSize * fontScale}px ...``) and read by packages/slides/src/model/layout.ts:444 and packages/slides/src/view/canvas/layout-preview.ts:38. The board twin has the same gap. So one peer writing `masters[0].placeholderStyles.body.fontSize = 1e9` bypasses every band this change adds. The write side agrees it is unguarded and says so on the wrong premise: packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:567-569 states "`masters` needs no walk … it carries no elements and no `Block`s, so there is nothing of this shape inside it" — true of `Block`s, false of the numerics that become one. Fix belongs on the new code (band `masters` on read, and/or walk `placeholderStyles` in `assertValidSlidesBody`).

samples.summary: `deckFontScale(meta.pxPerPt)` multiplies every banded slide font size at paint time with no ceiling, so a peer-written `meta.pxPerPt` defeats `MAX_FONT_SIZE` entirely.
samples.evidence: `deckFontScale` rejects non-finite and non-positive `pxPerPt` but has no upper bound: `return meta.pxPerPt / DOCS_PX_PER_PT;` (packages/slides/src/model/presentation.ts:139-144). It is applied to every text element, shape text, table and chart on the slide — packages/slides/src/view/canvas/element-renderer.ts:252 then 273/283/318/328/356/365 — and directly to the placeholder hint at packages/slides/src/view/canvas/text-renderer.ts:362. `meta` is peer-writable on the Yorkie root and is read through `migrateMeta` (packages/frontend/src/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.ts:481) with no band; the backend `assertValidSlidesBody` only checks the minimal meta shape (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:524-549). A `pxPerPt` of 1e9 turns a legitimately-banded 11 pt run into an ~8e9 px line, which is the same blank/huge-allocation render the new bands exist to prevent, reached by a field the change never touches.

samples.summary: The paste sanitizer was updated to agree with the CRDT readers on `fontSize`, `lineHeight`, `padding`, `rowHeights`, `listLevel` and image size — but not on `columnWidths`, which the readers now clamp to `MAX_COLUMN_RATIO`.
samples.evidence: `sanitizeTableData` still does `columnWidths.push(asNumber(rawWidths[c]) ?? 1 / cols)` (packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:333). `asNumber` only checks finiteness (clipboard.ts:81-83), so a pasted ratio of `1e9` is kept, while `parseColumnWidthsAttr` / `normalizeColumnRatio` clamp the same field to `[0, 1000]` on every CRDT read (packages/docs/src/model/numeric-attrs.ts:238-262, applied at crdt-tree.ts:222 and frontend yorkie-doc-store.ts:480) and the v1 slides PUT clamps it too. That is exactly the producer/reader divergence the file's own new comments say they are closing: the pasting client lays the table out 1e9× the content width, and after a reload the same document lays it out at 1000×.
searchedFor: read sanitizeTableData / sanitizeCell / asNumber in clipboard.ts

samples.summary: Truncating `tableData.columnWidths` to `MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS` without truncating `rows[].cells` violates the repo's documented `cells.length === numCols` invariant, which `normalizeTableMerges` derives from the *cells*, not from `columnWidths`.
samples.evidence: `bandOneBlock` does `table.columnWidths = (...).slice(0, MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS)` (packages/docs/src/model/numeric-attrs.ts:367) and the backend PUT does the same at packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:1056, leaving `rows[r].cells` at its original length. `normalizeTableMerges` computes `const numCols = td.rows[0].cells.length;` (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:695) and rebuilds the covered-cell markers over that grid, so after truncation the merge normalizer and `computeTableLayout` (`numCols = columnWidths.length`, packages/docs/src/view/table-layout.ts:153) disagree about the column count. docs/design/docs/... and packages/docs/src/import/docx-importer.ts:454-461 both treat `cells.length === columnWidths.length` as a load-bearing contract. Only reachable with a >256-column table, hence minor.

samples.summary: `parseColumnWidthsAttr` changes the result for an empty/absent `cols` attribute from `[0]` to `[]`, which makes `computeTableLayout` see `numCols === 0` and lay out no cells at all.
samples.evidence: The replaced expression was `(attrs.cols ?? '').split(',').map(Number).filter((n) => !isNaN(n))`; for a missing or empty attribute that is `['']` → `Number('') === 0` → `[0]` (length 1). The new helper short-circuits: `if (!attr) return [];` (packages/docs/src/model/numeric-attrs.ts:227). The same substitution was made in the second parser at packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:480. `columnWidths.length` is `numCols` in packages/docs/src/view/table-layout.ts:153, so a table node written with `cols: ''` (which `serializeTableAttrs` produces from an empty `columnWidths`, yorkie-doc-store.ts:356 / backend docs-tree.ts:155) now renders with zero columns instead of one degenerate column. Worth a deliberate decision rather than an accidental side effect of sharing the parser.

samples.summary: `assertValidSlidesBody` is now an in-place *mutator* as well as an assertion; an existing caller passes shared, module-level template-catalog objects to it purely as a validity check.
samples.evidence: packages/backend/src/template/seed/catalog.spec.ts:76 does `expect(() => assertValidSlidesBody(content.document)).not.toThrow();` over the seed catalog. Before this change the call was observationally pure; it now rewrites `content.document`'s `fontSize`/`lineHeight`/`listLevel`/`rowHeights`/`columnWidths`/spans in place (via `bandSlideBlockNumerics` / `bandSlideCellNumerics` / `normalizeSlideInlines`, packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:1022-1078,1203-1207). Any later assertion in the same process that reads the same catalog module sees the banded values. Harmless for trusted seeds, but the assertion signature no longer describes what the function does.

samples.summary: `Doc.setRowHeight` still stores an unclamped drag height while `computeTableLayout` now clamps it to `MAX_ROW_HEIGHT`, so the stored model and the rendered geometry can silently disagree.
samples.evidence: `setRowHeight` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:1177) writes the drag value straight into `tableData.rowHeights` and persists it via `updateTableAttrs`; the drag handler calls it per pointer move at packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2229. Step 5b now applies `normalizeRowHeight` at layout (packages/docs/src/view/table-layout.ts:256), so a height above 10000 px is stored but never rendered — the resize handle stops tracking the pointer and the value is quietly re-clamped on every later read boundary. The fix belongs on the new code (clamp at `setRowHeight` too, or accept and document the divergence).

verdict.reason: Every element of the claim checks out in the repo. `YorkieSlidesStore.read()` bands notes (yorkie-slides-store.ts:436), elements (:433-435 via bandElementText :505-520) and layouts (:456-458 via bandLayoutNumerics), but reads `masters` raw at :465. `Master.placeholderStyles` holds `fontSize`/`lineHeight` (master.ts:4-10,25-34), which `seedPlaceholderBlocks` copies verbatim into a docs Block's inline style and block style (placeholder-blocks.ts:30,38) — the exact pair `bandBlockNumerics`/`normalizeFontSize`/`normalizeLineHeight` clamp (numeric-attrs.ts:115-141,293-318). The same unbanded value is multiplied into a canvas font at text-renderer.ts:362 via element-renderer.ts:297-309, and consumed by layout.ts:442-453 and layout-preview.ts:38. It is peer-writable through the CRDT (`updateMaster`, yorkie-slides-store.ts:1075-1094; `cascadeMasterStyles` re-seeds blocks from it at :1122-1125), and the backend PUT validator explicitly skips masters on the premise that they contain no Blocks (docs-content.controller.ts:549-573, comment at :567-569). No migration or other guard normalizes master placeholder numerics (no fontSize/placeholderStyles/normalize matches in slides/src/model/migrate.ts). So a reachable peer-written path bypasses the band this change adds — a blast-radius finding (other consumer of a changed contract, outside the diff), not diff-internal logic.

It is applied to every text element, shape text, table and chart on the slide — packages/slides/src/view/canvas/element-renderer.ts:252 then 273/283/318/328/356/365 — and directly to the placeholder hint at packages/slides/src/view/canvas/text-renderer.ts:362. `meta` is peer-writable on the Yorkie root and is read through `migrateMeta` (packages/frontend/src/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.ts:481) with no band; the backend `assertValidSlidesBody` only checks the minimal meta shape (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:524-549). verdict.reason: Every claimed location checks out. `deckFontScale` (presentation.ts:139-144) guards only non-finite/non-positive `pxPerPt` and returns an unbounded ratio; element-renderer.ts:252 hands that factor to shape text (273/283), text (318/328), tables (356) and charts (365), and text-renderer.ts:362 multiplies the placeholder hint size by it directly. The multiplication happens AFTER the new band and is never re-banded: text-renderer.ts:267 calls scaleBlocks, autofit.ts:51 does `fontSize * scale`, and docs' layout.ts:124 consumes `style.fontSize` with no clamp (normalizeFontSize/MAX_FONT_SIZE at numeric-attrs.ts:115-118 only run at read/import/clipboard boundaries), so `already-guarded` fails. `pxPerPt` itself is unbanded on every ingress: migrate.ts:43-45 copies it with only isFinite + >0, readMeta uses it at yorkie-slides-store.ts:481-482, and the backend assertValidSlidesBody checks only meta.{title,themeId,masterId} (docs-content.controller.ts:536-548). It is reachable from untrusted data without any hand-written CRDT op: slides-view.tsx:252-263 writes the imported meta wholesale into the shared root, and import/pptx/index.ts:223-225 derives pxPerPt from `<p:sldSz cx>` with no ceiling, so a tiny cx yields an arbitrarily large scale. The diff's own comment (yorkie-slides-store.ts:498-502) names the exact harm the bands exist to prevent — a peer-written 1e9 font size hanging/blanking every other viewer's deck — which this unbanded multiplier reproduces. A reachable bypass of the change's new guard, located outside the diff: in-lane and major for the blast-radius rubric.

finding.summary: The board Yorkie store reads text bodies with no `bandBlockNumerics`, bypassing the new slides band on an identical code path
finding.evidence: `yorkie-board-store.ts:361` is documented as a "Verbatim port of `readElement` in `yorkie-slides-store.ts`", and line 374 reads `yorkieToPlain<Block[]>(rawData.blocks) ?? []` raw — no `bandBlockNumerics`, which the diff added to the slides twin (`yorkie-slides-store.ts:529`). The same gap exists at `yorkie-board-store.ts:1319` (`withTextElement`) and `:1351` (`priorText.blocks ?? []`), both banded on the slides side (`:2253`, `:2300`). Board elements are plain JSON on a peer-writable Yorkie root (no Tree attribute codec) and render through `boardToSlidesDocument` (`yorkie-board-store.ts:320`) → slides text renderer → docs `computeLayout`/`paginateLayout`. grep for `bandBlockNumerics` under `packages/frontend/src/app/board/` returns nothing, so a peer writing `fontSize: 1e9` / `rowSpan: Infinity` into a board sticky or text element still produces the hung/blank render this change exists to prevent.

verdict.reason: The absence claim is false at every location it cites. `packages/frontend/src/app/board/yorkie-board-store.ts:39` imports `bandBlockNumerics` from `@wafflebase/docs`, and all three allegedly-unbanded sites apply it: `readElement` reads `bandBlockNumerics(yorkieToPlain<Block[]>(rawData.blocks) ?? [])` at :383-385 (not the raw form quoted as evidence), `withTextElement` bands at :1333-1335, and `withShapeText` bands at :1368 (`const priorBlocks = bandBlockNumerics(priorText.blocks ?? [])`) — the exact line the finding quotes as missing the band. The doc comment at :363-368 states the read path is banded "exactly as the slides twin does". The sticky-note case is also covered: a sticky is a roundRect shape that falls through to the generic tail, which returns `bandElementNumerics({...})` at :442. The reviewer's own claim that grepping `bandBlockNumerics` under packages/frontend/src/app/board/ "returns nothing" is contradicted by the grep, which returns lines 39, 383, 1333 and 1368. No peer-written `fontSize: 1e9` / `rowSpan: Infinity` reaches `boardToSlidesDocument` unbanded via these paths.

finding.summary: Revision preview parses slides/board snapshots straight into `MemSlidesStore` with no band, so a poisoned deck hangs or blanks the preview
finding.evidence: `parseSlidesSnapshot` (snapshot-adapters.ts:44) is `unwrapYsonScalars<SlidesDocument>(YSON.parse(snapshot))` and `parseBoardSnapshot` (:61) feeds `boardToSlidesDocument`; neither applies `bandBlockNumerics`. `revision-preview.tsx:82/88` hands the result to `MemSlidesStore` (cf. `__tests__/snapshot-adapters.test.ts:127`), whose `read()` in `packages/slides/src/store/memory.ts` also does not band, and the deck is laid out by the same `computeLayout`/`paginateLayout` the diff calls a hang risk. The docs preview is safe (`parseDocsSnapshot` → `docsTreeToDocument`, banded by this change); the slides/board preview is the reader of the same stored bytes left out. Medium: I did not execute the preview to confirm the poisoned body reaches layout.

verdict.reason: The claimed gap does not exist. `parseSlidesSnapshot` (packages/frontend/src/components/history/snapshot-adapters.ts:52-56) returns `bandSlidesDocumentNumerics(unwrapYsonScalars<SlidesDocument>(YSON.parse(snapshot)))`, and `parseBoardSnapshot` (same file:71-88) wraps `boardToSlidesDocument(...)` in `bandSlidesDocumentNumerics(...)` at line 75 — banding after synthesis so the walk sees the synthetic slide. The import is at snapshot-adapters.ts:9. The band is a shared slides-level wrapper, `bandSlidesDocumentNumerics` in packages/slides/src/model/band-numerics.ts:104-123, which recurses through slide elements, shape/table/group bodies and speaker notes into `bandBlockNumerics` from @wafflebase/docs (band-numerics.ts:1,51,57,68,115), and is exported at packages/slides/src/index.ts:59-63. The reviewer's grep for `bandBlockNumerics` inside packages/slides/src would have shown these lines, and the module header (band-numerics.ts:12-19) names the revision-preview snapshot adapters as a required caller. MemSlidesStore not banding is moot because the document is already banded before it is stored.

finding.summary: `read()` bands slide elements and notes but not the `layouts` branch, whose placeholder specs carry the same `data.blocks` text bodies
finding.evidence: `yorkie-slides-store.ts:451` reads `const layouts = (root.layouts ?? []).map((l) => yorkieToPlain<Layout>(l));` with no band, while the sibling `slides` branch (:432-437) and `readElement` (:502-529, :608) were banded by this change. `Layout.placeholders: PlaceholderSpec[]` is `ElementInit & {...}` (`packages/slides/src/model/presentation.ts:52-63`) and a text placeholder init carries `data: { autofit, blocks }` (`packages/slides/src/model/layout.ts:35`); `staticElements: Element[]` on the same type can hold full text elements. Layouts are peer-writable (layout-edit mode, PPTX import) and their placeholder bodies are rendered in layout-edit mode and stamped into new slides, i.e. the same sink the band guards. Medium: I did not trace a layout placeholder body all the way into `computeLayout`.

verdict.reason: The finding claims read()'s `layouts` branch is unbanded. It is banded. yorkie-slides-store.ts:456-457 reads `const layouts = (root.layouts ?? []).map((l) => bandLayoutNumerics(yorkieToPlain<Layout>(l)));`, preceded by a comment (:452-455) stating precisely the rationale the finding argues for (placeholder specs are ElementInits with codec-free data.blocks, seeded into real elements on layout apply). The helper `bandLayoutNumerics` (packages/slides/src/model/band-numerics.ts:88-97) walks both `placeholders` and `staticElements` through `bandElementNumerics` (:46-80), which bands text `data.blocks`, shape `data.text.blocks`, table cell bodies, and recurses into groups with a depth cap. It is imported at yorkie-slides-store.ts:41 and exported from packages/slides/src/index.ts:61-63 and node.ts:60-62. The other document-level reader is covered as well: snapshot-adapters.ts:53,75 call `bandSlidesDocumentNumerics`, which bands `root.layouts` (band-numerics.ts:119-121). The reviewer's quoted source line does not exist in the working tree, so the absence claim fails on a single, directly cited counterexample.
